correctness.rationale: The finite-state process regenerates on returns to singleton e1. The first nonreset departure from e2 has probability (alpha+beta)/r for L=2 and alpha/r for L>=3; alternative success paths cost at least two rare nonreset steps. Each further extraction in a cycle requires an additional injection during O(1/r) vacancy intervals, giving geometric factorial-moment control and vanishing compound-event probability. Finite-state fast-state collapsing supplies uniform cycle moments. The marked-cycle triangular-array rare-event theorem yields J1 Poisson convergence at time rt. Regenerative reward/variance formulas yield V/J->1; generator calculations are supplementary.

value.rationale: Output counting statistics are a physically distinct high-value transport observable: equal rare stationary currents may coexist with bursty compound-Poisson extraction or super-Poisson fluctuations. The theorem rules out persistent extraction clusters, gives a universal shot-noise limit at all fixed finite lengths, and identifies an anomalous two-site intensity under identical protocol. It is not merely another stationary first-moment coefficient.
